structured_output.world_model:
W2 (empirical), after E051. Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0-2 (E036 + group-2 freeze over last 10% + 0.25 epoch top-up). Same-code reruns: E050 read 0.7552 at 5.206 s; E036 reruns read 0.7532/0.7525/0.7497/0.7544. Build noise is about 0.3 pp on a 3-seed mean and about ±0.03 s on time. Population mean is about 0.752, so headroom over the 0.75 bar is about 0.2 pp.

Mechanisms, with support:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.25 pp, roughly 1.5-2 s/pp (E020, E023, E027, E049).
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are already in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters were flat or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, wd, LS). Optimizer, averaging and regularization settings are flat within about 0.2 pp.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early 20 px is nearly free (E026, E033). Trimming steps or samples costs about as much as the dial (E031, E040, E041, E045, E048).
4. Backward truncation is the best lever (E028, E034, E036, E046, E049). It is bandwidth-heavy. The group-2 freeze saves about 0.2-0.25 s at roughly neutral accuracy. Freezing at 60% is a cliff (E037, -0.38 pp). E039 and E042 saved only 0.03-0.05 s.
5. Architecture cuts cost accuracy at about the dial's rate or worse. E021 narrowed group 2 and lost 0.25 pp. E010 narrowed group 3 and lost 0.25 pp. E051 (stride-2 conv replacing conv+pool) saved 0.29 s (-5.6%) but lost about 0.7 pp, so it is a bad trade. Removing the nonlinearity or capacity at the stem hurts.
6. Non-step overhead is about 2.5% (E047). Systems work recovers at most about 1% (E035).
7. Noise: the 3-seed std is about 0.15-0.2 pp, and a rebuild alone moves the mean by 0.3 pp, so single-run differences under 0.3 pp are not resolvable. The kept tip is probably a lucky draw.

Misses: I under-predicted the savings of cuts and freezes (E046, E048). E043 was rebuild noise. I over-predicted time-neutral boosters.

Unsure:
- Whether ReLU saves 3% or more. I expect about 1-3%, because the fused kernels are bytes-bound but erf may not be fully hidden. I also expect a small accuracy cost of 0.1-0.3 pp.
- Whether the freeze can go earlier than 90% for group 2 without a cliff. E037's cliff was for group 1, so group 2 may be more forgiving, but its accuracy contribution is likely larger.
- Whether loss-based selection beats the dial. It looks about equal.

forecasts.reason: GELU to ReLU likely saves ~2% of time via fewer bytes and cheaper erf; accuracy shift within noise, maybe slightly negative.
Selection plus top-up is roughly dial-neutral; net steps nearly equal, so time ~ tip and accuracy ~ tip within noise.
Extra 13 frozen steps save ~0.1 s (~10 ms each); accuracy likely loses ~0.1 pp, near the cliff edge but unresolved at 3 seeds.

cruxes: Does ReLU's saved-bytes and erf saving reach 3% of step time, or is the fused BN/activation traffic bytes-bound so it saves only 1%?
Is the true population mean of the tip above 0.752, and can a rebuild's kernel reselection be pinned? Without this, sub-0.3 pp keep decisions are noise.
Is group-2 freeze dose (85% vs 90%) on a cliff like E037's group-1 freeze, or still on the flat part?
